title: Global Accelerator anycast entry and AWS global network
thesis: Two anycast static IPs route TCP/UDP from nearest edge into the AWS network, then to healthy regional endpoints.
diagram: Draw clients in two geographies -> same two anycast addresses -> edge -> regional ALBs. Distinguish global edge ingress from HTTP content cache.
remember: Static entry points and regional endpoints are separate decisions.

title: Global Accelerator listener, endpoint groups and health
thesis: Standard accelerator listener protocol/ports, regional endpoint groups, traffic dials, endpoint weights and health checks.
diagram: Draw listener -> two regional endpoint groups -> ALB/NLB/EC2/EIP. Healthy endpoint selection and failover for new connections; client-IP preservation depends on endpoint type/configuration.
remember: Traffic dial is a share of traffic already directed to that Region, not a global split.

title: Global Accelerator versus CloudFront
thesis: Both enter AWS global edge; CloudFront serves HTTP(S) content and can cache; Global Accelerator proxies TCP/UDP to regional applications with static IPs.
diagram: Large five-row comparison matrix: protocol, cache, endpoint, fixed IP, failover; miniature side-by-side flow below.
remember: Use Global Accelerator for non-HTTP or static IP/regional failover; CloudFront for HTTP content delivery.

title: CloudFront request path and cache hierarchy
thesis: Viewer request to edge cache; cache hit returns at edge; miss may traverse regional cache to origin; separate request and response arrows.
diagram: Large cache hit/miss branch with icon for CloudFront, Regional Edge Cache and origin. Add Shield/WAF as security overlays, not cache stages.
remember: Cache hit avoids origin; miss and uncacheable paths still benefit from edge connectivity.

title: CloudFront origin types and protocol contract
thesis: S3 REST origin with OAC; S3 website endpoint as custom HTTP origin without OAC; ALB, EC2, API Gateway and other HTTP origins; media origins.
diagram: Decision tree keyed on origin type, HTTPS support and access control.
remember: An S3 website endpoint is a custom origin and cannot use OAC.

title: Private S3 origin with OAC and policy
thesis: CloudFront OAC signs requests to private S3 REST endpoint; bucket policy scopes SourceArn to distribution; KMS policy when SSE-KMS.
diagram: Viewer -> CloudFront -> signed origin request -> private S3 with bucket policy; show direct S3 request denied.
remember: OAC secures the origin; viewer authorization is a separate control.

title: CloudFront caching versus S3 replication
thesis: Edge TTL-based caching worldwide versus S3 replication to chosen Regions; propagation, storage, update and use cases differ.
diagram: Two equal architecture diagrams plus comparison table, no numbering.
remember: Choose CDN for global reads, replication for regional copies and residency or recovery.

title: ALB and EC2 custom origin reachability
thesis: Publicly reachable CloudFront custom origin endpoint; ALB can route to private EC2 targets; security group and origin request protocol.
diagram: CloudFront -> public ALB -> private EC2 instances, with explicit Internet-facing ALB; alternate public EC2 origin.
remember: CloudFront cannot directly use a private EC2-only endpoint as an ordinary custom origin.

title: Restrict direct ALB origin access
thesis: CloudFront-managed prefix list in ALB security group and a secret custom origin header checked by ALB listener rule; origin protection is layered.
diagram: Diagram attack path direct ALB blocked and CloudFront path allowed; small control matrix.
remember: A secret header alone is not a complete network boundary.

title: Origin group failover contract
thesis: Primary/secondary origin group; configured status codes and connection timeout; only GET/HEAD and cached OPTIONS eligible.
diagram: Large failure sequence: cache miss -> primary failure -> secondary; inset ineligible POST/PUT path.
remember: Failover is per eligible request, not a permanent regional switch.

title: CloudFront geographic restrictions
thesis: Distribution country allowlist/blocklist uses GeoIP; distinguish coarse content restriction from robust user authorization.
diagram: Map-style regions with allowed/blocked examples and viewer request policy decision.
remember: Geo restriction is country-based and does not replace authentication or licensing logic.

title: Price class and delivery-cost choices
thesis: Price Class All, 200, 100 trade edge coverage and potential latency for cost; data transfer/request prices vary by geography and commitment.
diagram: Three-column price class table and conceptual reach map without exact prices.
remember: Price class changes the set of serving edges; assess latency and actual traffic geography.

title: CloudFront signed URL and signed cookies
thesis: Application authenticates viewer then signs URL/cookie with private key; CloudFront validates via trusted key group public key before cache/origin.
diagram: Sequence with app signer -> viewer -> CloudFront trusted key group -> OAC private S3; signed cookie for multiple objects inset.
remember: Trusted key groups replace obsolete root-account key pair advice.

title: CloudFront signed URL versus S3 presigned URL
thesis: CloudFront authorization and cache/path policy versus S3 SigV4 request signed by principal; origin exposure and delivery differ.
diagram: Large table with path, signer, caching, expiry, IP/date restrictions and origin control; short two flows.
remember: CloudFront signature protects distribution access; S3 presign grants a specific S3 API request.

title: Custom errors and error caching
thesis: Map selected origin 4xx/5xx to custom response page/status; Error Caching Minimum TTL and monitoring may affect recovery.
diagram: Origin error -> CloudFront custom error policy -> S3 custom page -> viewer; preserve separate true origin status in logs.
remember: Custom errors improve experience but can mask origin health if monitored only by viewer status.

title: Cache key, TTL and invalidation
thesis: Cache policy decides headers/cookies/query strings in cache key, min/default/max TTL; origin request policy can forward data without adding to key; versioned URLs or invalidation refresh stale content.
diagram: Key composition equation on left, hit/miss branch on right, short operational refresh panel.
remember: Forwarding a value and including it in the cache key are distinct choices.

title: Edge function event lifecycle
thesis: Viewer request/response at edge and origin request/response on misses; functions alter request/response but do not provide storage cache themselves.
diagram: Four-event event-order timeline with cache-hit short path and origin-miss long path.
remember: Origin events do not run on a cache hit.

title: CloudFront Functions viewer events
thesis: Lightweight JavaScript at viewer request or response for header, URI, redirect and JWT-like validation; runtime 2.0 KeyValueStore; no network/file system/request body.
diagram: One dominant viewer-edge path with a compact capability/limit table, no 3 steps.
remember: Use Functions for short viewer-side logic; publish LIVE before association.

title: Lambda@Edge four triggers and replication
thesis: Node.js/Python published version in us-east-1 replicated globally; viewer/origin request and response; network/body capabilities subject to restrictions.
diagram: Timeline with four trigger anchors and origin-miss boundary, regional edge cache label; version deployment callout.
remember: Viewer and origin trigger semantics differ, especially on cache hits.

title: Combining Functions with Lambda@Edge
thesis: CloudFront Function viewer event may pair with Lambda@Edge origin event, but cannot pair with Lambda@Edge viewer event on same behavior.
diagram: 2x4 allowed/blocked matrix and one valid combined path.
remember: Check cache-behavior/event association conflicts before deployment.

title: When Lambda@Edge is necessary
thesis: Choose Lambda@Edge when origin event, network call, request body, longer execution or third-party library is needed; otherwise Functions often fit viewer changes.
diagram: Decision tree with branches for origin event, body/network, lightweight viewer.
remember: Use the least complex edge runtime that satisfies the actual event and capability.

title: CloudFront Functions versus Lambda@Edge limits
thesis: Compare runtime, trigger, location, network/file/body, memory and execution quota; avoid older fixed numeric limits unless verified.
diagram: Large readable capability table using checkmarks and footnote current quotas vary; official service icons.
remember: Feature support and trigger placement drive selection more reliably than stale quota snapshots.

title: Edge code use cases and cache-key normalization
thesis: Functions: URI/header transforms, redirects, token checks, cache-key normalization. Lambda@Edge: body, origin logic, network, libraries.
diagram: Four original mini workflows arranged 2x2 with practical input-output examples.
remember: Normalize before cache lookup to avoid unnecessary cache variants.

title: Authentication at the edge
thesis: Viewer token validation at viewer request, protected origin via OAC or origin controls; distinguish function denial and origin authorization.
diagram: JWT verification sequence with valid/expired branches and cache placement.
remember: An edge auth check must validate signature, expiry, audience and policy, not only decode a token.

title: User-Agent content adaptation
thesis: Inspect User-Agent or supported device hints and rewrite URI for mobile image, avoiding cache collisions; origin may hold variants.
diagram: Desktop/mobile bifurcation into distinct cache keys and objects with response labels.
remember: Cache key must vary with transformed resource identity, or users may receive the wrong variant.

title: Global application and dynamic API path
thesis: CloudFront distributes static S3 content and accelerates dynamic API requests; Lambda@Edge logic can modify routing; DynamoDB access is through application API, not direct edge cache.
diagram: Static branch cache hit S3; dynamic branch CloudFront -> regional API/Lambda -> DynamoDB.
remember: Do not treat dynamic application data as static cached content without an explicit policy.

title: Lambda@Edge origin selection
thesis: Origin-request Lambda@Edge on cache miss may select a different configured S3 origin; permissions, DNS/host header and cache behavior matter.
diagram: Cache miss -> origin-request Lambda@Edge -> S3 origin A/B with geo/business rule; show S3 replication separately.
remember: Origin-request selection runs only when CloudFront forwards to origin.

title: CloudFront, Global Accelerator and Route 53 selection
thesis: DNS routing, HTTP CDN cache and TCP/UDP anycast acceleration solve different layers; combine when architecture calls for them.
diagram: Large three-service purpose/traffic/health/static-entry table, with small layered example.
remember: A DNS response is not itself an edge content cache or packet proxy.

title: Cache update and observability workflow
thesis: Versioned asset path, cache-policy TTL, invalidation and cache-hit/error metrics; inspect logs and origin response when stale or failing.
diagram: Before/after timeline of deployment, old cache, invalidation/versioned URL and validation.
remember: Prefer versioned asset URLs for repeatable releases; invalidate when a stable URL must change.

title: Walkthrough: private S3 via CloudFront OAC
thesis: Create private S3 origin and OAC, scope bucket policy, use viewer controls, test CloudFront success and direct S3 denial, clean up.
diagram: Illustrative console view with 4 sequential actions and evidence/results; no live AWS execution claim.
remember: Test both allowed distribution access and denied direct origin access.

title: Walkthrough: ALB origin failover and error path
thesis: Configure primary/secondary origin group, failover status, GET test, ALB origin control and error response; verify POST does not fail over.
diagram: Illustrative configuration/evidence screenshots with 4 actions, not generic 3 cards.
remember: Origin group failover eligibility and direct-origin restriction must be tested separately.

title: Walkthrough: Global Accelerator regional failover
thesis: Create standard accelerator, listener, endpoint groups and healthy ALBs; test stable IPs and region failure, monitor new-connection rerouting, cleanup.
diagram: Illustrative endpoint health and traffic flow, step numbers only for actual operations.
remember: Static anycast IPs remain while endpoint selection responds to health.
